The statement balances robust labor conditions and elevated inflation with reassurance that the banking system is “sound and resilient.” However, the latest SLOOS points to broad-based tightening in credit that likely amplifies the statement’s caution: banks report tighter standards for C&I and CRE loans; weaker demand across nonfarm nonresidential, construction/land development, and multifamily; and reduced financing needs for plant/equipment, M&A, inventories, and receivables. Foreign banks also report weaker C&I demand. These survey signals reinforce the FOMC’s expectation of tighter credit conditions weighing on activity and hiring and heighten downside risks, particularly around CRE and credit quality.

Financial stability risks flagged in the FSR—persistent inflation pressures, Treasury market liquidity strains, and leveraged loan/CRE vulnerabilities—are consistent with the SLOOS backdrop. Policy implementation remains supportive of market functioning (IOER 4.9%, ON RRP 4.8%, standing repo 5%, and ongoing balance-sheet runoff), which tempers tail risks but does not offset the expected credit drag.

Net tone: more cautious than previously assessed. Adjusting for SLOOS-confirmed credit tightening and softer loan demand, the overall assessment shifts from slightly negative to modestly negative.
